IS : 6213( Part IX ) - 1973

Indian Standard
METHODS OF TEST FOR PULP
PART IX BLEACH REQUIREMENTS AND PREPARATION OF HAND SHEETS FOR OPTICAL TESTS OF PULP

0.
0.1 This Jndian

FOREWORD

Standard ( Part IX ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 March 1973, after the draft finalized by the Paper Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 For obtaining good quality of paper, it is essential that the pulp which goes into the manufacture of paper is properly cooked and bleached. Formulation of this standard had been taken up in order to guide the people working in pulp and paper mills for the methods to be adopted for pulp analysis. 0.3 To control the optical properties of the paper it is essential to know the extent of cooking carried out of the pulp. It is also essential to find out the requirement of the bleach liquor necessary to attain a certain This standard lays down the procedure for estimatdegree of brightness. ing the bleach requirement of the pulp and the details of a rapid method for preparation of hand sheets for carrying out optical tests. This method is applicable to all types of pulps which can be bleached with calcium hypochlorite solution.

1s : 6213 ( Part IX ) - 1973 2.2 Procedure 2.2.1 Take a representative sample of the pulp. Tear the sheet into pieces and defibre mechanically. Determine the dry contents of the sample. Weigh out 5 portions, each equivalent to 10 f 0.1 g of moisture free pulp. Determine the permanganate number of another portion of the sample. Half of this value of permanganate number will give the approximate requirement of chlorine for bleaching.
2.2.2 Place each weighed portion of the pulp in 1-litre polyethylene jars. Mix thoroughly with distilled water by means of the stirrer to give a conCarefully measure out bleach liquor in steps sistency of about 2 percent. For of about 0.5 percent, above and below the estimated requirement. example, if the estimated requirement of available chlorine is 10 percent on the mass of the pulp, then measure out bleach liquor corresponding to Dilute these 9.0, 9.5, 10.0, 10.5 and 11.0 percent available chlorine. samples of bleach liquor with enough distilled water so that when added to the pulp samples in polyethylene jars ( 2 percent consistency ) the final consistency of the pulp samples in each jar is 1.24 to l-26 percent of dry pulp. Cover the jars with lids and place them in a thermostatic bath at 55 f 1�C. Allow the bleaching to continue, keeping the pulp agitated by' occasionally manually shaking the jars. Test the supernatant liquor with starch iodide paper for presence of chlorine. Wash the pulps from different jars, make standard sheets as given in 3.2.1 and determine the brightness. 3. 3.0 General - This method provides rapid means for preparing hand sheets with bleached and unbleached pulps for optical tests, provided the pulp fibres are or can be separated.

Dilute the specimen with distilled water so that the are well separated. Fit the buchuer funnel with slurry contains 2 g of dry pulp per litre. filter paper and wet it with distilled water from a wash bottle. Apply suction rnomentari!y to seat the filter paper and -pour 1.000 ml of pulp Apply suction till the excess water has been removed. slurry in the funnel. Then turn off the vacuum line and remove the funnel immediately so that air is not drawn lhrough the sheet. 3.2.2 Lay two filter papers on the press and invert the buchner funnel Transfer the pulp sheet by blowing from the neck. over the press. Cover the pulp sheet with two or more blotting papers. Put the cover of the press and screw two of the diagona~Iy opposite wing nuts. Raise the pressure to 345 K.N/mz ( approximately 3"5 kgf/cm* ) in 30 seconds and maintain it for 5 minutes. Release the pressure and remove the press cover. Fit the sheet into a set of drying rings. Dry the sheet in an After the atmosphere with reiative humidity not more than 65 percent. Remove sheets are thoroughly dry, remove them from the drying rings. the filter paper and test the sheets for optical properties. 4.
